source.snippet: We have a managed package (1GP) that Successfully packaged, Upgraded successfully in majority of subscriber orgs. Yet, a couple customers ran into the following error: Deployment Failure — Expression is too long, please split this expression into multiple statements. Retrying the upgrade eventually worked in orgs that hit that error which was interesting - as that seems to indicate there's no deterministic error here. How can we identify expressions that are at risk of hitting this limit?

problem_statement: Salesforce ISV partners building managed packages cannot reliably identify which Apex expressions will trigger non-deterministic 'expression too long' compilation errors during subscriber org upgrades, causing failed deployments and customer-facing incidents.
target_segment: Salesforce ISV developers and AppExchange partners maintaining managed packages (1GP/2GP) with large enterprise subscriber bases
notes: ISV context means this is a business problem with paying customers affected. Static analysis tooling that pre-identifies Apex expressions at risk of hitting governor limits before packaging would have clear commercial value. Salesforce ISVs pay for AppExchange security reviews and dev tooling. Niche but high-value segment — a Salesforce-focused linting/CI plugin could address this.
